item.title: _Overview
item.description:
The ten time cycles in Kittens Game, which are named after space missions, each have a unique astronomical symbol or glyph that appears to the left of your current year.

Here are the glyphs for each of the cycles:

  1. Charon: ⍙
  2. Umbra: ⍦
  3. Yarn: ⍧
  4. Helios: ⌒
  5. Cath: ⌾
  6. Redmoon: ⍜
  7. Dune: ⍫
  8. Piscine: ⎈
  9. Terminus (T-minus): ⍝
  10. Kairo: ℣

Understanding the Glyph Colors

Each cycle lasts for five years. The active glyph will dynamically change color to let you know exactly which year of the current cycle you are in:

Understanding the Glyph Colors

Each cycle lasts for five years. The active glyph will dynamically change color to let you know exactly which year of the current cycle you are in:

  • 🔴 Red: Year 0
  • 🟡 Orange-Yellow: Year 1
  • 🟢 Green: Year 2
  • 🔵 Blue: Year 3
  • 🟣 Violet: Year 4

Once you research the Numerology and Numeromancy metaphysics upgrades, these cycles will actively alter your space structures’ production rates and grant powerful, unique bonuses whenever you hold festivals.

item.title: Piscine Cycle
item.description:
The Piscine cycle is the eighth in the sequence of ten five-year cycles in the Kittens Game time system. It is represented by the glyph ⎈ and provides specific modifiers to space production and festivals once late-game Metaphysics are researched.

Cycle Mechanics and Effects

The modifiers for the Piscine cycle are active only after researching specific Metaphysics technologies:

  • Numerology Effects: Researching Numerology activates production modifiers for space-based structures, acting as a “boom” period for starcharts but a “fallow” period for advanced catnip production:
    • Research Vessels: Starchart production is increased by +50%.
    • Hydroponics: Catnip production is reduced by -50%.
  • Numeromancy (Festival) Effects: If a festival is held during this cycle and Numeromancy is researched, the village receives a x2 multiplier (doubled income) for Science.

Relationship to Planet Piscine

The cycle is named after the planet Piscine, described as a gigantic aquatic planet with an acid body and a methane atmosphere.

  • Numeromancy (Festival) Effects: If a festival is held during this cycle and Numeromancy is researched, the village receives a x2 multiplier (doubled income) for Science.

Relationship to Planet Piscine

The cycle is named after the planet Piscine, described as a gigantic aquatic planet with an acid body and a methane atmosphere.

  • Piscine Mission: Reaching the planet requires 1,500 starcharts, 9,000 titanium, 200,000 science, and 250 kerosene.
  • Research Vessel: Completing the mission unlocks the ability to build Research Vessels. Each vessel provides +10,000 science storage and produces 0.05 starcharts per second.

Strategic Importance

The Piscine cycle and the associated planet are critical for mid-to-late game progression:

  • Solving Starchart Bottlenecks: Research Vessels are considered the earliest “best” way to generate starcharts. Because these vessels receive a 50% production boost during the Piscine cycle, it is the most efficient window to accumulate the starcharts needed for high-tier missions.
  • Science Farming: The 2x festival bonus to science income makes this cycle an ideal time to stockpile science for expensive late-game technologies or for crafting large quantities of Compendiums and Blueprints.
  • Food Warning: Players must be cautious of the -50% penalty to Hydroponics catnip production. While this rarely causes starvation in the late game due to massive terrestrial production bonuses, it can reduce the surplus available for wood refinement.

item.title: Helios Cycle
item.description:
The Helios cycle is the fourth in the sequence of ten five-year cycles within the Kittens Game time system. Represented by the glyph ⌒, it repeats every 50 years, beginning at Year 15 of every millennium (e.g., Years 15–19, 65–69, etc.).

Cycle Mechanics and Effects

The modifiers for the Helios cycle are only activated once specific late-game Metaphysics technologies have been researched:

  • Numerology Effects: Researching Numerology activates modifiers for energy and space storage:
    • Sunlifter: Energy output is increased by +50%.
    • Cryostations: Storage capacity is reduced by -10%.
  • Numeromancy (Festival) Effects: If a festival is active during this cycle and Numeromancy is researched, your village receives significant bonuses to religion-based resources:
    • Faith income x2 (doubled).
    • Unicorn income x1.25.

Space Exploration Context

The cycle is named after the star Helios, a G2V spectral type star at the center of the Cath solar system. Reaching it requires the Helios Mission, which is unlocked after the Dune mission and costs 3,000 starcharts, 15,000 titanium, 250,000 science, and 1,250 kerosene. Completing this mission unlocks several critical late-game structures:

    • Faith income x2 (doubled).
    • Unicorn income x1.25.

Space Exploration Context

The cycle is named after the star Helios, a G2V spectral type star at the center of the Cath solar system. Reaching it requires the Helios Mission, which is unlocked after the Dune mission and costs 3,000 starcharts, 15,000 titanium, 250,000 science, and 1,250 kerosene. Completing this mission unlocks several critical late-game structures:

  • Sunlifter: Generates Antimatter (1 per year) and high energy (30 Watts base).
  • Containment Chamber: Increases maximum antimatter storage.
  • Heatsink: Enhances the storage capacity of Containment Chambers by +2% and increases their power consumption.
  • Sunforge: Provides a +1% bonus to the storage capacity of all base metals (iron, titanium, gold, uranium, and unobtainium).

Strategic Importance

  • Energy Maximisation: Because Sunlifters receive a +50% production boost during this cycle, it is one of the best times to run energy-intensive infrastructure, such as high numbers of AI Cores or Entanglement Stations.
  • Religion Farming: The doubled faith income from festivals makes the Helios cycle an ideal window for “Praising the Sun” to maximize the Solar Revolution bonus or for pushing toward higher Transcendence Tiers.
  • Storage Penalties: Players must be cautious of the -10% penalty to Cryostation storage. Since Cryostations are one of only two buildings that provide Unobtainium storage, this cycle can temporarily lower your resource cap, which may cause you to lose surplus unobtainium if you are near your maximum capacity.
  • Antimatter Production: While some early strategy guides consider Helios missions a low priority, acquiring Sunlifters is mandatory for entering the Relic era, as they are the primary source of the antimatter needed for Relic Stations.

item.title: Kairo Cycle
item.description:
The Kairo cycle is the tenth and final five-year cycle in the Kittens Game time system. Represented by the glyph ℣, it repeats every 50 years (Years 45–49, 95–99, etc.).

Cycle Mechanics and Modifiers

The effects of the Kairo cycle are only active if you have researched specific Metaphysics technologies:

  • Numerology Effects: This technology activates several production and science modifiers for space-based structures, primarily acting as a “fallow” period for general production but a massive boom for starcharts:
    • Space Elevators: Their transferred production bonus is reduced by -50%.
    • Satellites: Starchart production and the science bonus provided to Observatories are both reduced by -25%.
    • Space Stations: Their science bonus is reduced by -25%.
    • Space Beacons: In contrast to the penalties above, their starchart production is boosted by +400%.
  • Numeromancy (Festival) Effects: If a festival is held during this cycle and Numeromancy is researched, your village receives a massive x5 multiplier to starchart income.

Relationship to Space Exploration

The cycle is tied to the Kairo Mission, which is required to reach the dwarf planet Kairo at the edge of the solar system.

Relationship to Space Exploration

The cycle is tied to the Kairo Mission, which is required to reach the dwarf planet Kairo at the edge of the solar system.

  • Mission Requirements: Reaching Kairo requires 5,000 starcharts, 20,000 titanium, 300,000 science, and 7,500 kerosene.
  • Space Beacon: Once Kairo is reached, you can construct Space Beacons. These structures are the primary beneficiary of the cycle’s modifiers, providing significant starchart generation and expanded science limits.

Strategic Importance

The Kairo cycle is the ultimate window for farming starcharts in the late game. While the penalties to Space Elevators and Satellites can temporarily slow down general resource production and unobtainium gathering, the combination of the +400% Space Beacon boost and the x5 festival bonus allows players to accumulate the massive starchart reserves needed for high-tier missions like Centaurus or for building large fleets of Trade Ships.

Advanced players often use a Chronoforge to skip through less productive cycles to land in Kairo when they need to break a starchart bottleneck.

item.title: Umbra Cycle
item.description:
The Umbra cycle is the second of ten five-year cycles in the Kittens Game time system. Represented by the glyph ⍦, it begins at Year 5 of every millennium and repeats every 50 years (Years 5–9, 55–59, etc.).

Cycle Mechanics and Modifiers

The effects of the Umbra cycle are only active once specific late-game Metaphysics technologies have been researched:

  • Numerology Effects: This technology activates modifiers for space-based structures, primarily those located on the planet Dune and the Umbra black hole:
    • HR Harvester (Umbra): Energy production is increased by +50%.
    • Hydraulic Fracturer (Dune): Oil output is reduced by -25%.
    • Planet Cracker (Dune): Uranium output is reduced by -10%.
  • Numeromancy (Festival) Effects: If a festival is held during this cycle and Numeromancy is researched, your village receives a 1.5x income multiplier for four critical industrial resources: Coal, iron, titanium, and gold.

Relationship to Space Exploration

The cycle is tied to the Umbra Mission, which involves reaching a supermassive black hole at the heart of the Helios system.

Cycle Mechanics and Modifiers

The effects of the Umbra cycle are only active once specific late-game Metaphysics technologies have been researched:

  • Numerology Effects: This technology activates modifiers for space-based structures, primarily those located on the planet Dune and the Umbra black hole:
    • HR Harvester (Umbra): Energy production is increased by +50%.
    • Hydraulic Fracturer (Dune): Oil output is reduced by -25%.
    • Planet Cracker (Dune): Uranium output is reduced by -10%.
  • Numeromancy (Festival) Effects: If a festival is held during this cycle and Numeromancy is researched, your village receives a 1.5x income multiplier for four critical industrial resources: Coal, iron, titanium, and gold.

Relationship to Space Exploration

The cycle is tied to the Umbra Mission, which involves reaching a supermassive black hole at the heart of the Helios system.

  • Mission Requirements: Reaching Umbra requires 25,000 starcharts, 500,000 science, 25,000 kerosene, and 15,000 thorium.
  • HR Harvester: Once reached, you can build HR Harvesters, which generate energy from black hole evaporation. These structures are significantly more efficient during the Umbra cycle.

Strategic Context

  • Energy Maximisation: In the deep late game, players often rely on HR Harvesters for power. Because these receive a 50% boost during the Umbra cycle, it is the most stable time for energy-heavy operations, such as running high numbers of AI Cores or Entanglement Stations.
  • Fallow Industrial Period: For players farming Unobtainium, the Umbra cycle is generally considered a “fallow” or less profitable period. Advanced players often use a Chronoforge to skip through both the Charon and Umbra cycles to reach the more lucrative Redmoon cycle, which provides massive bonuses to unobtainium production.
  • Metal Stockpiling: Despite being a “skip” year for space minerals, the 1.5x festival bonus to basic metals makes it a useful time for mid-game players to refill their stocks of titanium and gold for terrestrial building projects.

item.title: Terminus Cycle
item.description:
The Terminus cycle (often referred to in tables as the T-minus cycle) is the ninth in the sequence of ten five-year cycles within the Kittens Game time system. Represented by the glyph ⍝, it repeats every 50 years (beginning at Year 40 of a millennium, then Year 90, 140, etc.).

Cycle Mechanics and Effects

The effects of the Terminus cycle are activated only after researching specific Metaphysics technologies:

  • Numerology Effects: Researching Numerology activates production and storage modifiers for space-based structures:
    • Sunlifter: Energy output is reduced by -50%.
    • Cryostations: Storage capacity is increased by +20%.
  • Numeromancy (Festival) Effects: If a festival is held during this cycle and Numeromancy is researched, the village receive a 2x multiplier (doubled income) for Oil.

Space Exploration Context

The cycle is named after the planet Terminus, which is reached through the T-minus Mission.

Space Exploration Context

The cycle is named after the planet Terminus, which is reached through the T-minus Mission.

  • Planet Description: Terminus is described as a supermassive ice giant located at the far end of the Helios solar system.
  • Mission Requirements: Reaching it requires 2,500 starcharts, 12,000 titanium, 225,000 science, and 750 kerosene.
  • Unlocks: Completing the mission unlocks the Kairo Mission, the Cryostation structure, and access to the T-Minus planet.

Strategic Importance

In the late game, the Terminus cycle is highly valued for its bonus to Unobtainium storage capacity:

  • UO Cap Scaling: Because Cryostations are one of only two structures that provide Unobtainium storage, the +20% storage bonus from this cycle is essential for players attempting to reach the 8.14 billion Unobtainium cap needed to build 100 Chronospheres.
  • Oil Management: The 2x festival bonus makes this cycle an ideal time to stockpile oil, especially when preparing to build expensive space structures like Research Vessels.
  • Energy Warning: Players must be cautious of the -50% penalty to Sunlifter energy output during this cycle, which can lead to a sudden energy deficit and global production penalties if their grid is not sufficiently diversified.

Represented by the glyph ⍫, it repeats every 50 years (starting at Year 30 of a millennium, then Year 80, 130, etc.). Its primary function is to significantly boost industrial outputs related to the planet for which it is named.

Cycle Mechanics and Effects

item.content:encoded:
The Dune cycle is the seventh in the sequence of ten five-year cycles within the Kittens Game time system. Represented by the glyph ⍫, it repeats every 50 years (starting at Year 30 of a millennium, then Year 80, 130, etc.). Its primary function is to significantly boost industrial outputs related to the planet for which it is named.

Cycle Mechanics and Effects

Like other cycles, Dune’s effects are activated only after researching specific late-game Metaphysics technologies:

  • Numerology Effects: This technology activates modifiers for space-based structures located on the planet Dune and the Umbra black hole:
    • Planet Crackers: Uranium output is increased by +10%.
    • Hydraulic Fracturers: Oil output is increased by +50%.
    • HR Harvesters: Energy production is reduced by -25%.
  • Numeromancy (Festival) Effects: If a festival is held while the Dune cycle is active and Numeromancy is researched, your village receives a 2x multiplier (doubled income) for Uranium.

Relationship to Planet Dune

The cycle is tied to the Dune Mission, which is unlocked after the Moon Mission. Reaching Dune requires 1,000 starcharts, 7,000 titanium, 175,000 science, and 75 kerosene. Once reached, you can construct the structures affected by the cycle’s modifiers:

  • Planet Cracker: The primary source of automated Uranium production.
  • Hydraulic Fracturer: Provides a high-pressure stream of Oil.
  • Spice Refinery: Refines sand into Spice, a rare resource that improves happiness.

Strategic Importance

The Dune cycle is a critical window for resource management in the late mid-game and early space eras:

  • Uranium Farming: Uranium is essential for powering Reactors, funding Nuclear Smelters (for titanium), and fueling Lunar Outposts (to produce unobtainium). The 2x festival bonus makes this cycle the most efficient time to stockpile uranium.
  • Oil Stabilization: Because Hydraulic Fracturers receive a 50% production boost during this cycle, it is an ideal time to fill your oil caps to build expensive space structures like Research Vessels or Moon Bases.
  • Energy Management: Players heavily reliant on HR Harvesters for power (common in the deep late game) must be wary of the -25% energy penalty during this cycle, which could lead to an energy deficit and global production penalties.
  • Progression Flow: In the sequence of cycles, Dune acts as a mirrored opposite to the Umbra cycle, which penalizes Dune structure output while boosting Umbra structures. Shattering Time Crystals is often used to skip Umbra and land in cycles like Dune or Redmoon to maximize resource yield.

item.title: Charon Cycle
item.description:
The Charon cycle is the first in the sequence of ten five-year cycles within the Kittens Game time system. Each cycle is associated with a specific glyph and provides production modifiers or festival bonuses once certain late-game Metaphysics technologies are researched.

Cycle Mechanics and Effects

The effects of the Charon cycle are only active after researching specific Metaphysics technologies:

  • Numerology Effects: Researching Numerology activates modifiers for space-based structures during this cycle:
    • Lunar Outposts: Unobtainium output is reduced by 10%.
    • Entanglement Stations: Gigaflops consumption is increased by 100%.
  • Numeromancy (Festival) Effects: If Numeromancy is researched, holding a festival during the Charon cycle provides a 1.5x multiplier to the income of three basic resources: Catnip, wood, and minerals.
  • Visual Indicator: The cycle is represented by the glyph ⍙. The color of this glyph changes annually to indicate progress through the five-year period: red (Year 0), orange-yellow (Year 1), green (Year 2), blue (Year 3), and violet (Year 4).

Relationship to Space Exploration

The cycle is named after the planet Charon, which is the destination of a high-tier late-game space mission.

Relationship to Space Exploration

The cycle is named after the planet Charon, which is the destination of a high-tier late-game space mission.

  • Charon Mission: Unlocked after the Umbra mission, it requires 75,000 starcharts, 750,000 science, 35,000 kerosene, and 35,000 thorium.
  • Planet Charon: Described as an incredibly dense dwarf planet at the edge of the Helios system, sometimes called “The Gates of Death”.
  • Entanglement Station: Once Charon is reached, you can construct Entanglement Stations, which generate hashes for reverse-engineering relics but consume significant energy and gigaflops. As noted above, their gigaflops consumption is doubled during the Charon cycle.

Strategic Context

In the late game, the Charon cycle is generally considered a “fallow” period for industrial production, particularly because of the penalty to unobtainium output from Lunar Outposts. Advanced strategies for farming unobtainium often involve using a Chronoforge to skip through the Charon and Umbra cycles to reach more profitable years, such as those in the Redmoon cycle. Conversely, if a player is still in the early-to-mid game and needs to build up stocks of wood or minerals, the Numeromancy festival bonus makes Charon a useful time to run festivals.

item.title: Yarn Cycle
item.description:
The Yarn cycle is one of the ten five-year cycles in the Kittens Game time system. Each cycle is associated with a specific glyph and provides various production modifiers and festival bonuses once certain late-game technologies are researched.

Cycle Mechanics and Effects

The effects of the Yarn cycle become active only after researching specific Metaphysics technologies:

  • Numerology Effect: When Numerology is researched, the Yarn cycle provides a +100% boost to catnip production from Hydroponics. Conversely, it imposes a -50% penalty to starchart production from Research Vessels.
  • Numeromancy Effect: If Numeromancy is researched, holding a festival during the Yarn cycle results in doubled culture income (x2).
  • Timing: As the third cycle in the sequence, it begins at Year 10 of a millennium and repeats every 50 years (Years 10–14, 60–64, etc.).

Space Exploration Context

The cycle is named after the planet Yarn, a Class M planet with a moderate climate and oxygen atmosphere.

The cycle is named after the planet Yarn, a Class M planet with a moderate climate and oxygen atmosphere.

  • Mission: The Yarn Mission is unlocked after the Helios mission and requires 7,500 starcharts, 35,000 titanium, 350,000 science, and 12,000 kerosene.
  • Planet Structures: Once reached, you can build Terraforming Stations (which increase your maximum kitten population by +1) and Hydroponics systems.
  • Hydroponics: These structures provide a +10% bonus to maximum catnip and a +2.5% boost to catnip production. During the Yarn cycle, this production bonus is significantly enhanced by the Numerology modifier.

Strategic Importance

In the extreme endgame, terraforming Yarn is a key strategy for maximizing kitten population. By building a massive number of Terraforming Stations, players can reach population levels high enough to generate “unreasonable” amounts of Paragon (up to 120,000 per RL-day) during long runs. Additionally, the cycle’s festival bonus makes it an ideal time to grind culture if you are still using it for early-to-mid-game crafts like Manuscripts or Compendiums.

item.title: Redmoon Cycle
item.description:

Its primary purpose is to provide a massive multiplier to Unobtainium production, which is the critical bottleneck for space exploration and time manipulation.

The character used for the Redmoon cycle is the glyph ⍜.

Core Effects

item.content:encoded:
The Redmoon cycle is the sixth phase in the ten-cycle system of Kittens Game and is widely considered the most strategically important period for late-game resource farming. Its primary purpose is to provide a massive multiplier to Unobtainium production, which is the critical bottleneck for space exploration and time manipulation.

The character used for the Redmoon cycle is the glyph ⍜.

Core Effects

The impact of the Redmoon cycle depends on your researched Metaphysics upgrades:

Upgrade Required Effect during Redmoon
Numerology +20% Unobtainium output from Lunar Outposts.
Numerology -50% Gigaflop consumption for Entanglement Stations.
Numeromancy Holding a festival provides an additional x2 Unobtainium income.

The “Shatter into Redmoon” Strategy

Because the Redmoon cycle is so much more productive than other cycles, endgame players use Time Crystals to skip less profitable years and land exactly on the Redmoon phase.

  • Timing: The first Redmoon cycle begins at Year 25 and lasts for five years (approximately 66.67 minutes of real-time play).
  • The Shatter Engine: By “shattering” (combusting) Time Crystals in the Chronoforge, players can advance the calendar instantly. It takes 45 skips to get from the end of one Redmoon cycle back to the start of the next one.
  • Maximising Returns: Strategic guides recommend staying in Redmoon as much as possible to fuel the “Type 0 Relic Engine”. When combined with Breweries, the festival bonus in Redmoon can reach nearly 2.5x total production.

Why It Matters for Progression

The Redmoon cycle is the foundation of the self-sustaining positive chrono-reset loop.

  • Unobtainium Accumulation: Players need billions of Unobtainium to build the 70+ Chronospheres required to carry over enough resources to make a reset profitable.
  • Arbitrage: By timing their most intensive production and trading (specifically with the Elders/Leviathans) during Redmoon, players can generate the massive amounts of Unobtainium and Time Crystals needed to reach the Endgame.

item.title: Cath Cycle
item.description:
The Cath cycle is the fifth of ten cycles in the Kittens Game temporal system, following the Helios cycle and preceding the Redmoon cycle. Each cycle lasts for five game years (20,000 ticks), which translates to approximately 1 hour, 6 minutes, and 40 seconds of real-time.

Indicators and Identification

  • Glyph: The cycle is identified by the ⌾ symbol appearing to the left of the year in the calendar.
  • Color Coding: The color of the glyph changes to denote the specific year within the five-year Cath cycle: Red (Year 0), Orange-Yellow (Year 1), Green (Year 2), Blue (Year 3), and Violet (Year 4).

Resource Multipliers (Requires Numerology)

  • Glyph: The cycle is identified by the ⌾ symbol appearing to the left of the year in the calendar.
  • Color Coding: The color of the glyph changes to denote the specific year within the five-year Cath cycle: Red (Year 0), Orange-Yellow (Year 1), Green (Year 2), Blue (Year 3), and Violet (Year 4).

Resource Multipliers (Requires Numerology)

If you have researched the Numerology metaphysics upgrade, the Cath cycle provides specific bonuses and penalties to space-based production:

  • Space Elevators: Provides a +100% bonus to the transferred production bonus, specifically for Oil.
  • Satellites: Provides a +100% bonus to starchart production and a +100% bonus to the Satellite observatory science bonus.
  • Space Stations: Provides a +50% bonus to science production.
  • Space Beacons: Imposes a -50% penalty to starchart production.

Festival Effects (Requires Numeromancy)

When the Numeromancy metaphysics upgrade is researched, holding a Festivals during the Cath cycle grants a unique global modifier:

  • Catpower Boost: All Catpower income is doubled (x2) for the duration of the festival. This effect can be further enhanced by building Breweries.

Strategic Utility

In the late game, players often use the Chronoforge to “shatter” Time Crystals, skipping through less desirable cycles to reach those that benefit their current bottleneck. While Redmoon is often the primary target for Unobtainium farming, the Cath cycle is strategically valuable for players needing to maximize Oil transfer via Space Elevators or those looking to quickly cap Science through boosted Satellites and Space Stations. Additionally, the doubled Catpower income from festivals makes Cath an ideal time for mass trading or hunting.
